text:
li: Quick question — for the new console quickfilter, should 'filters stick to model' or 'stick to route' by default? This changes telemetry attribution and saved query UX.

nina: leaning model-first because users expect model-specific performance breakdowns. But i'm worried about cross-route queries being surprising.

sam: model-first makes rollout simpler: we can tag telemetry with model_id. Route-first needs per-route overrides + extra index in query store.

kevin: from a UI pov, model-first means filter pill shows model badge, and saved queries can default to model scope. route-first keeps pins persistent per-route though.

morgan: design prototypes show both. Proposal: dropdown default = 'scope: model' but show a banner: "filter applies to model across routes" with an opt-out toggle.

li: what about quotas and cost? If model scope aggregates traffic, telemetry sampling may undercount route spikes.

sam: we can surface a per-scope telemetry multiplier in analytics and warn on quota impacts. e.g., show "Projected token delta: +12%" before saving.

kevin: snippet of how saved_query payload would look:
```
{
  "name": "Recent llm errors",
  "scope": "model", // or "route"
  "filters": {"status":"error"}
}
```

nina: rollout plan: A/B 10% model-default vs 10% route-default, check retention and save rates, and track 'save_scope_mismatch' metric.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled to staging at 2025-09-30T18:00Z for feature-flag gated rollout :rocket: 

li: ok lets add a telemetry field for 'saved_scope' and a flag 'user_overrode_scope' so we can do post-hoc analysis. I'll add to product spec.

sam: i'll add backend support for scope + quota delta calculation. Kevin can you wire the UI warning when projected delta >5%?

kevin: yep. I'll stub the banner and the tooltip copy. :thumbsup:

nina: thanks all — tagging @morgan for polish on banner copy and @li for the spec. We'll sync tomorrow quick.
